variants.name: POSIX AIO with a sigevent value as the token
variants.implementation_notes: The portable realization: the token is a pointer you define (typedef void *ACT) and hand to the runtime inside the request's control block. aio_read/aio_write store the operation in a struct aiocb whose aio_sigevent field names the notification: with SIGEV_SIGNAL the token arrives as siginfo.si_value in the handler, with SIGEV_THREAD sigev_value is passed as the callback's sole argument - i.e. the completion is pushed back together with the token. Dispatch is one cast plus a call, with no lookup of the response by request identity.
pitfalls: The aiocb and the buffer it references must stay valid and unchanged until the operation completes; running two asynchronous operations through one aiocb is undefined (aio(7)).
glibc's POSIX AIO is a user-space thread-pool emulation, so a callback still costs a thread - the very cost the token pattern is meant to avoid at high request counts.
A void* token that is never returned (service failure, operation abandoned) leaks whatever it references; keep a registry/index so it can be reclaimed.

variants.name: Linux kernel AIO / libaio with io_event.data
variants.idiom_name: struct iocb.aio_data returned in struct io_event.data
variants.implementation_notes: The kernel fast path is a completion queue rather than a callback: aio_data in the request (struct iocb) is copied verbatim into the data field of struct io_event when the I/O completes, and the client pulls completions in batches with io_getevents. The token never touches a thread, only the request and the returned event, which is what makes it scale to many outstanding operations on one context. libaio wraps the raw io_setup/io_submit/io_getevents system calls; the interface is Linux-specific, not POSIX.
pitfalls: Completion events must be reaped; an unreaped event queue silently loses both the result and the token it carried.
The interface is Linux-only and its semantics have shifted (io_uring for new code); do not present it as portable C.
aio_data is a raw 64-bit register: a truncated or forged value from the completion queue dispatches the wrong state, so validate it against a registry before use.
